title: Orthonormality of product functions
statement: Let $\Omega$ and $I$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on $\Omega$, and let $B=(b_a)_{a\in I}$ be a real basis of functions on $\Omega$ orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $\pi$, with one basis function constantly equal to $1$. For a natural number $n$ and indices $a,b\in I^n$, the inner product of the corresponding product functions under the product distribution $\pi^n$ is $1$ if $a=b$ and $0$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: Finite nonempty index set $I$ with decidable equality
A real basis of functions on $\Omega$
The distinguished basis vector is constantly $1$
The basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
